span.label: A formal category is collapsed into a different one on the basis of how voters behave, not on the rule that defines it: semiopen-list systems are treated as closed-list because voters in practice choose the preordered list.
span.note: what this limits: the candidate-centred versus party-centred classification of electoral systems: semiopen-list systems are placed with closed-list ones because of observed voter behaviour rather than the rule
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The key explanatory variable is measured by proxy, and the reason given is endogeneity rather than validity: the observed quantity would be caused by the thing being explained.
span.note: what this limits: the conflict variable as a measure of conflict in the vote at hand: it is a proxy, adopted because conflict observed in a particular vote is endogenous to the vote decisions being explained
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: One side of the model is assumed non-strategic, and the assumption is adopted because the quantity involved is endogenous.

span.label: semiopen-list PR systems —same-as→ closed-list
span.note: differs in: NOTHING THAT MATTERS TO THE OUTCOME, WHICH IS THE POINT: the two are formally distinct - semiopen lists let voters express a preference for individuals - but 'because parties control who gets elected, most semiopen-list PR systems are, IN PRACTICE, very similar to closed-list PR systems'. The formal distinction survives; the behavioural one does not · strength of the relation: 0.8 — A FORMAL CATEGORY COLLAPSED INTO ANOTHER ON THE EVIDENCE OF PRACTICE, and the record already carries both readings as senses of `electoral system` - AS FORMAL RULE and AS PRACTICE. The analysis then treats the merged class as one, so every downstream coefficient depends on this move.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: policy conflict —operationalised-as→ roll-call votes
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — THE PROXY IS CHOSEN OVER THE DIRECT MEASURE FOR A STATED REASON, AND THE REASON IS ENDOGENEITY: the two variables are 'PROXY MEASURES of policy conflict … This, however, is PREFERABLE to using OBSERVED conflict in each vote because conflict in a particular vote is ENDOGENOUS to the MEPs' vote decision.' The observable quantity is rejected precisely because it is downstream of what is being explained - a rare case of a proxy defended rather than apologised for.

span.label: MEPs elected under institutions that weaken their national party's grip — a candidate-centered electoral system, decentralized candidate selection, and large district magnitude — are less likely to vote against their European party group.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same three institutions push in the opposite direction for the other principal: candidate-centered voting rules, decentralized candidate selection, or a large district each make an MEP more likely to vote against her own national party.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: For defection from the national party the two institutions do not add up independently: only the combination of a candidate-centered system with decentralized selection raises defection, since either a party-centered system or centralized selection alone is enough to suppress it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Longer service in the European Parliament lowers defection from the European party group but raises defection from the national party.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Domestic constitutional design — semipresidentialism in France and federalism in Germany — does not carry over into MEP voting behaviour, since MEPs from both countries defect less than average from their national parties.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Defection is rare overall: MEPs almost always voted with the majorities of both their European party group and their national party.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: National parties enforce their voting instructions best where the rules give them strong control, namely closed-list PR, small districts, or centralized candidate selection; where the rules are open-list PR, large districts, or decentralized selection, MEPs side with their European party group instead.
